question: Should the generic tool-progress kind and predicate become the durable public plugin-SDK contract for transient progress payloads?
rationale: Upstream Codex supports the lifecycle distinction, but exposing it as shipped third-party API is a permanent compatibility and ownership choice that automation cannot safely make.

options.title: Approve generic progress intent
options.body: Keep the closed generic marker and predicate, then enforce them consistently across every Slack delivery representation with contract tests.

options.title: Keep the seam internal
options.body: Move tool-progress classification behind an internal runtime boundary and avoid expanding third-party plugin API in this fix.

recommendation.title: Approve generic progress intent
recommendation.body: Keep the closed generic marker and predicate, then enforce them consistently across every Slack delivery representation with contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans both affected Slack and plugin-SDK boundaries, making this the best available owner for the permanent API choice.
